rationale.text: A standard external EMD is intended to remain compatible across compliant refrigerator brands.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall obtain logger data and optional operating power through the M2M interfaces defined by WHO/PQS/E006/DL01.3 without requiring a refrigerator-specific adapter.

rationale.text: Prolonged mounting can prevent the logger from recording new data objects.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall release a mounted logger USB data interface no later than 180 seconds after initiating the mount.

rationale.text: This association permits the remote service to convert logger-relative timing into absolute event time.

statement.text: At each logger download, the monitoring device shall record its synchronized UTC time and associate that time with the logger identity and relative timestamp of the downloaded records.

rationale.text: Automatic synchronization avoids relying on clinic personnel to maintain the absolute clock.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall synchronize its UTC clock automatically from the remote service often enough that displayed device time differs from service time by no more than one minute while communication is available.

rationale.text: Local staff must be able to relate displayed events to local operating records.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall allow an administrator to configure a local time zone and shall display on-site timestamps in that local time zone.

rationale.text: A browser or mobile device may be unavailable during the event that needs local attention.

statement.text: The monitoring device display shall show current refrigerator temperature, alarm state, fault state, alarm-monitoring enablement, and estimated remaining device-energy days without use of a separate computing device.

rationale.text: Both modalities increase the chance that an on-site user notices the event.

statement.text: Upon detecting a configured alarm condition, the monitoring device shall immediately present an unmistakable visual indication and an intermittent audible indication of at least 70 dB(A) at one metre.

rationale.text: Audible muting is a human-factors action, not evidence that the triggering condition ended.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall let an on-site user mute the audible indication for the current alarm without clearing the visual indication, recorded alarm, or remote alarm state.

rationale.text: A persistent indication reduces the risk that a refrigerator returns to service with alarms unintentionally disabled.

statement.text: When local alarm monitoring is disabled, the monitoring device shall continuously show the disabled state until monitoring is re-enabled.

rationale.text: A local backlog permits reconstruction of the remote history after connectivity returns.

statement.text: While the remote communication path is unavailable, the monitoring device shall retain each acquired logger record and each generated alarm or fault event until the remote service acknowledges receipt.

rationale.text: Recovery should not depend on a clinic user noticing that connectivity has returned.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall automatically reconnect to its configured remote communication path after an interruption and resume transmission of current and retained records.

rationale.text: The environmental condition makes the independence claim testable at the source specification's severe temperature.

statement.text: Starting with fully charged internal energy storage, the monitoring device shall perform its allocated acquisition, recording, display-on-demand, alarm, and communication functions for at least 240 hours without external power at 43 degrees Celsius.

values.title: Operate for 240 hours without supplied power

rationale.text: Energy conservation may reduce routine transmissions but must not hide state transitions.

statement.text: During loss of supplied power, the monitoring device shall detect each alarm condition within 15 minutes and shall immediately attempt remote transmission whenever an alarm or fault state changes.

values.title: Report alarm changes during power loss

rationale.text: Monitoring must not impose an excessive load on the refrigerator power interface.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall draw no more than 5 watts from the refrigerator M2M power connection.

rationale.text: Persistent codes permit a technician to diagnose an intermittent or previously cleared fault.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall retain locally accessible codes for EMD and connected-logger faults for at least 60 days after each fault is detected.

rationale.text: Energy-storage service should not create unrelated calibration work or require product return.

statement.text: A trained technician shall be able to replace each designated replaceable energy-storage component on site without recalibrating the refrigerator logger sensors.

rationale.text: The selected device is externally mounted in a potentially dusty, humid clinic environment.

statement.text: The installed monitoring-device enclosure shall provide at least IP64 protection as defined by IEC 60529.

rationale.text: Preserving the source bytes avoids device-specific reinterpretation before remote ingestion and integrity checking.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall transmit each downloaded logger file to the remote data service without modifying the file contents.

rationale.text: The remote service needs a value established before transfer in order to detect transfer corruption.

statement.text: The monitoring device shall calculate and transmit a SHA-256 digest for each downloaded logger file before transmitting that file to the remote data service.

rationale.text: Local awareness supports timely programme action and must not depend on wide-area connectivity.

statement.text: Clinic personnel need to recognize current refrigerator conditions, temperature excursions, and monitoring faults while they are at the storage site.

rationale.text: Remote awareness supports oversight and escalation across geographically separated service points.

statement.text: Authorized public-health programme staff need to learn of refrigerator alarm and monitoring-fault conditions without visiting the clinic.

values.title: Remote awareness of alarms and faults

rationale.text: The selected deployment context includes intermittent electricity and communications.

statement.text: Clinic personnel need monitoring and local alarming to continue during prolonged loss of site power and temporary loss of remote connectivity.

rationale.text: A current indication alone cannot support trend review, excursion investigation, or demonstration of prior conditions.

statement.text: Authorized users need retained time-correlated monitoring, alarm, and fault records sufficient to investigate excursions and equipment performance.

rationale.text: Hosting the data outside the clinic must not transfer programme ownership or grant unrestricted access.

statement.text: The employer needs to control who can access its raw and summarized monitoring data throughout the contracted service period.

rationale.text: Interoperability permits equipment and data-service choices to remain separable.

statement.text: The employer needs the monitoring product to interoperate with compliant refrigerator loggers and external programme data systems without proprietary reinterpretation of cold-chain records.

rationale.text: Field service reduces avoidable monitoring outages at remote clinics.

statement.text: A trained service technician needs to diagnose monitoring faults and replace serviceable energy-storage components at the deployment site.

rationale.text: Investigation and coordination require events from different systems to share an understandable time basis.

statement.text: Authorized users need monitoring records from logger-relative time to be associated with trustworthy absolute time and displayed in the configured local time zone.

rationale.text: Missing evidence must not be presented as evidence of acceptable storage conditions.

statement.text: Authorized users need to distinguish unavailable readings, communication interruptions, and device faults from measured in-range conditions.

rationale.text: Product monitoring is only one input to the programme's documented excursion-response process.

statement.text: Clinic personnel need monitoring information to support, but not automate, decisions about whether vaccines remain suitable for use after an excursion.

values.title: Preserve human authority over vaccine disposition

rationale.text: The content and deadline make the remote-awareness obligation observable at the product boundary.

statement.text: Within 15 minutes after the monitoring device detects an alarm, SVEMS notification delivery shall submit a notification containing equipment identity, alarm type, event time, and current status to each configured external recipient endpoint while that endpoint is reachable.

rationale.text: Gateway acceptance is distinguishable from assumed human receipt and makes delivery failure investigable.

statement.text: SVEMS notification delivery shall record whether each configured external gateway accepted or rejected each notification request and shall expose that outcome to authorized users.

rationale.text: Automatic reconnection and retry must not corrupt trend or alarm counts with duplicates.

statement.text: The remote data service shall accept a retransmitted logger file or generated record without creating a second logical observation or event when its equipment identity, record identity, and recorded time equal an already accepted item.

rationale.text: The hosted service is the durable remote record for the employer's changed service period.

statement.text: The remote data service shall retain accepted raw observations, logger files, alarm events, fault events, configuration changes, and generated summaries for at least five years after their recorded time.

rationale.text: Programme and service roles require different access to potentially sensitive equipment information.

statement.text: The remote data service shall authenticate each user and shall allow data access or administration only for equipment and operations assigned to that user's authorization.

rationale.text: Recording before application preserves an audit fact even if downstream configuration delivery fails.

statement.text: Before applying an administrative change, the remote data service shall record the authenticated user, UTC time, affected configuration item, previous value, and requested new value.

rationale.text: A corrupted file should remain visible as a fault rather than silently entering the historical record.

statement.text: The remote data service shall verify the integrity value supplied for each logger file and shall mark the file unavailable for operational use when verification fails.

rationale.text: A complete export makes employer data portable and independently analyzable.

statement.text: For an authorized export request, the remote data service shall produce a documented machine-readable package containing every retained raw observation, alarm, fault, and summary whose recorded time falls within the selected interval.

rationale.text: A recipient can use the digest to detect accidental alteration or truncation after export.

statement.text: The remote data service shall provide a SHA-256 digest over each exported package and identify the digest algorithm in the export response.

rationale.text: A durable interval classification supports both browser presentation and historical investigation of missing data.

statement.text: For each configured observation interval, the remote data service shall classify its status as received, awaiting delayed communication, unavailable from the logger, or affected by an identified monitoring fault using received records and device-status events.

rationale.text: The system cannot display, alarm on, or transmit observations that it has not acquired within the source recording interval.

statement.text: SVEMS shall acquire each available time-based refrigerator data object from the connected logger at least once every 15 minutes.

rationale.text: The logger supplies relative time, so SVEMS must establish the absolute-time association used remotely.

statement.text: SVEMS shall associate each downloaded logger record with UTC derived from an independently synchronized clock whose displayed time differs from server time by no more than one minute while synchronization is available.

rationale.text: These values let clinic personnel distinguish normal operation, excursions, faults, and intentionally disabled alarming.

statement.text: SVEMS shall present current refrigerator temperature, active alarm state, active fault state, monitoring-enabled state, and EMD energy remaining at the storage site.

rationale.text: An on-site alarm must be apparent without requiring a browser or remote network.

statement.text: When SVEMS detects a configured alarm condition, it shall immediately activate a locally apparent visual alarm and a 70 dB(A) or greater audible alarm measured at one metre.

rationale.text: The delay bound connects local event detection to useful remote oversight while acknowledging an external network dependency.

statement.text: SVEMS shall make a detected alarm condition known to configured remote recipients no later than 15 minutes after the alarm condition begins while an external communication path is available.

rationale.text: The selected external EMD must remain useful through long refrigerator holdover periods.

statement.text: Following loss of refrigerator-supplied power, SVEMS shall continue data acquisition, recording, local alarm detection, local alarm annunciation, and alarm-status communication for at least 240 hours.

values.title: Continue essential operation without supply power

rationale.text: Local monitoring continuity is insufficient if the remote historical record remains permanently incomplete after connectivity returns.

statement.text: After restoration of its configured remote communication path, SVEMS shall reconnect automatically and transmit records accumulated during the interruption without duplicating or discarding an accumulated record.

rationale.text: Standardized and unmodified data supports interoperability and independent downstream interpretation.

statement.text: SVEMS shall represent acquired and generated cold-chain data objects in the format defined by WHO/PQS/E006/DS01.2 and shall preserve downloaded logger files unmodified when transmitting them to the remote data service.

rationale.text: The employer's changed service period supports a longer programme audit and investigation horizon.

statement.text: SVEMS shall make raw observations, alarms, faults, and derived summaries available to authorized employer users for at least five years after their recorded time.

rationale.text: Hosted monitoring should not expose clinic or equipment information to unrelated users.

statement.text: SVEMS shall restrict remote monitoring data and administrative operations to authenticated users authorized for the applicable employer equipment.

rationale.text: Data ownership is operationally meaningful only if the employer can retrieve and use its information outside the hosted interface.

statement.text: SVEMS shall allow an authorized employer user to export all raw observations, alarms, faults, and summaries for a selected time interval in a documented machine-readable form.

rationale.text: Explicit status prevents a missing reading from being interpreted as an in-range reading.

statement.text: For each expected observation interval, SVEMS shall distinguish a received observation, an interval awaiting communication, an unavailable logger observation, and an identified monitoring fault.

rationale.text: Investigation must distinguish equipment behavior from changes in the configuration used to interpret or communicate it.

statement.text: SVEMS shall record the time, authenticated actor, previous value, and new value for changes to equipment identity, time zone, alarm thresholds, alarm enablement, recipient assignments, and user authorization.

rationale.text: The monitoring product lacks the product, exposure, and programme authority needed to make a disposition decision.

statement.text: SVEMS shall not classify monitored vaccines as acceptable, unusable, or releasable and shall label excursion information as input to the employer's response process.

rationale.text: Distinct persistent codes support restoration of monitoring without requiring the technician to infer the failed boundary.

statement.text: SVEMS shall provide a trained technician with persistent diagnostic codes for EMD, logger-interface, power, and remote-communication faults.

rationale.text: Undetected transfer or export corruption could make an historical record misleading.

statement.text: SVEMS shall detect accidental alteration or truncation of each transferred logger file and each exported monitoring-data package.

rationale.text: Presenting value, time, and status together avoids making stale or unavailable data appear current.

statement.text: The browser interface shall show the latest received temperature, its recorded time and receipt status, active alarms, active faults, and a time-ordered history for equipment authorized to the user.

rationale.text: The system boundary must remain apparent where users interpret excursion data.

statement.text: The browser interface shall label every excursion display and export as monitoring information that does not determine vaccine disposition.
